title: Notes and sources for each arena's construction, renovations, tax status and lease

rows.public_construction_notes: 3% car-rental tax paid for $62.5M of public infrastructure (Bond Buyer: $70.7M car-rental-tax bonds sold 1996, refunded 2005). Arena itself financed by $130.75M Recreation Authority bonds repaid by Turner ($12.5M/yr) -> treated as private (conduit). Time Warner $20M toward infrastructure.
rows.conduit_note: Recreation Authority arena bonds repaid by Turner/arena revenues (c, Marquette via search; Bond Buyer reports $147.5M taxable 1997)
rows.bond_detail: 2017 City of Atlanta and Fulton County Recreation Authority Serie $110M not confirmed
rows.lease_terms: Non-relocation to 2046 (matches bond maturity)
rows.exit_penalty: Break-up fee up to $200M before 2046; Hawks pay $5.9M/yr lease after bonds retire 2028

rows.construction_cost_other_reports: Developer's "Total Cost" at opening, scope not defined (FCE 10-K FY2012). Alternatives: $890.2M recorded building cost with land at zero (b, same 10-K Schedule III; includes capitalized interest, amount not given); $940.0M recorded at Dec 31 2014 after post-opening work (b); pre-opening estimates $904.3M-$911.1M (b, FCE 10-Ks FY2009-FY2011); ~$1.0B (c, Wikipedia)
rows.public_construction_notes: City capital contribution "has grown from $100 million to $205 million" (b, IBO testimony May 2009) + State $100M (b, IBO fiscal brief Sept 2009 p.2: "direct payments of $100 million each from the city and state"; also Doctoroff via Gotham Gazette, c). Alternative for the city: $150M, because IBO's Sept 2009 brief (p.3) counts only about half of the $105M addition, $50M, as caused by the project (b), for land acquisition and infrastructure for the arena block, outside the arena cost. MTA Vanderbilt Yard: IBO (Sept 2009) puts the subsidy at the $50M gap between Extell's $150M cash bid and Forest City's $100M and attributes $10M (present value) of it to the arena, using the 2009 terms' $20M of $100M for the arena block (b) -> land bucket (a public asset sold below the competing bid). Extell's $150M is computed from IBO's $50M gap (a). Whole-project alternatives, not counted: $50M bid gap (b); IBO's $214M appraisal ($214.5M per Atlantic Yards Report, c) minus the $100M present value of the 2009 payment stream at the MTA's 6.5% = $114.0M (a); replacement yard cut from $240-250M (MTA CFO via Atlantic Yards Report, c) or $182M (developer's figure via Atlantic Yards Report, c) to $147M (b, MTA staff summary) = $35M-$103M (a). The $10M is a present value as of FY2010 but is deflated with the construction money at the 2012 opening year (at 2010 it would be about $0.7M higher in 2026 dollars).
rows.pilot_note: Tax-exempt PILOT bonds (2009; refunded 2016 as $478.7M tax-exempt + $15M taxable) repaid from PILOTs in lieu of property tax (would-be tax $99M vs PILOT $39M in 2023 per IBO). Counted only in the expanded total.
rows.bond_detail: 2009 Brooklyn Arena Local Development Corp PILOT bonds $564M tax-exempt | 2016 BALDC PILOT Revenue Refunding Bonds Series 2016A $478.665M tax-exempt | 2016 BALDC PILOT Revenue Refunding Bonds Series 2016B $15M TAXABLE
rows.lease_terms: Non-relocation agreement cited by Moody's as PILOT-bond credit positive; PILOT bonds final debt service 2046
rows.exit_penalty: Term/penalty not confirmed

rows.construction_cost_other_reports: BRA-approved estimate: "The total capital required to complete the Project is estimated to be $160,000,000" (Report and Decision); the Application says the $160M is "inclusive of pre-development and property acquisition costs" (1992); $161.9M arena-only projection incl. $23.1M construction-period interest, taxes, loan fees and linkage (b, team-filed 1990 Draft Project Impact Report Table IV-1); $160M (c, Wikipedia); no as-built cost found
rows.public_construction_notes: No public construction money found. Financed by a $120M bank loan and $40M developer equity (BRA 1992); the Commonwealth paid compensation for taking the developer's 150 Causeway St leasehold (not a subsidy). Approved as a Chapter 121A project with negotiated tax payments of $1.0M a year rising $0.1M a year to $1.5M, which the BRA called necessary for the financing (not quantified as a break). The 1993 House bill had the developer repay $5.126M of MBTA work by a note starting in year 11 (deferred, not a grant; enacted text not checked).
rows.lease_terms: Lease through 2035-36 season (2021 15-yr extension)
rows.exit_penalty: Not public

rows.construction_cost_other_reports: City ACFR: "The $200 million project" (not itemized). $265M (c, Carolina Journal); $260M (c, Charlotte Observer via SBD; Wikipedia); $182M (c, Athletic Business); $200M (2002 plan). The $60-65M gap may be land, parking or financing costs; no document reached says so
rows.public_construction_notes: City ACFR FY2020: the project "was funded primarily through a combination of installment financing obligations supported by a portion of an occupancy tax and a dedicated rental car tax, private contributions and the sale of City assets" (b, no amounts). Carolina Journal: taxpayers ~$170M, owner Johnson ~$23M (c). 2002 plan also had banks/utility underwrite $100M recovered ~$50M via sale of city land, a 3% seat tax (~$15M) and $16.8M F&B rights. $170M used as the explicitly attributed figure.
rows.ongoing_notes: City arena maintenance reserve contributions beyond the $0.6M a year counted in the 2014 deal, net of the Hornets' match: Arena Maintenance Reserve (tourism taxes) less the Hornets' contribution, less $0.6M a year already in the 2014 row; actual budget years FY2020-23; FY2024-26 net zero; FY2006-19 not reachable
rows.bond_detail: 2003 City of Charlotte COPs $229M tax-exempt | 2023 City of Charlotte variable-rate COPs (converted 2024) $110M not confirmed
rows.lease_terms: Extended from 2030 to 2045 (council vote of 10-1, June 13 2022)
rows.exit_penalty: City was already obligated to spend $173M under the old lease; the Hornets pay a total of $32M in rent through 2045 (start year not stated) and continue a $1.1M-a-year capital fund contribution (WBTV); under the 2005 lease the rent was a capital amount of $250,000 rising to $500,000 (Marquette summary)

rows.public_construction_notes: Privately financed. The 1989 state law (P.A. 86-110) valued the arena by a formula (20% of 4 x owners' net income after interest, income taxes and capital repairs) with a $1M minimum tax, for 22 years after the base year; taxes forgone 2002-2016 estimated at $46.6M nominal (expanded total only; 1994-2001 not computed). 2024 Board of Review cut AV from $92.1M to $50.3M on owner appeal.
rows.tax_break_desc: 1989 stadium valuation formula (P.A. 86-110; 35 ILCS 200/10-205 to 10-220), tax years through 2016 (end inferred)
rows.tax_break_notes: Taxes forgone 2002-2016 at the first post-formula assessment ($32.31M AV, 2017) x each year's equalizer and rate, minus taxes paid: $46.6M nominal (a, from Assessor, PTAXSIM and IDOR data); $36.1M at the 2021 market value; about $77M if extended to 1994-2001 (rough); a floor because 1994-2001 inputs were not reachable
rows.lease_terms: Team-affiliated owner; no public lease
rows.exit_penalty: n/a

rows.construction_cost_other_reports: Recorded cost of the arena building incl. allocated joint costs, excluding land, shared site work ($40.2M for the complex) and capitalized interest and other construction-period costs ($23.7M for the complex) (Gateway FY1999 balance sheet "Arena 157,816,726"). ~$198.5M with a pro-rata share of those shared items (a, illustrative); $152M (c, PFM); $148M (c, SBD Dec 1994); $100M (c, Wikipedia); whole Gateway complex $425.0M (b)
rows.public_construction_notes: Gateway FY1999 audit Note 7D: Cuyahoga County issued $75M (1992) and $45M (1994) of taxable economic development revenue bonds and lent the proceeds to Gateway "to pay Arena construction costs" ($120M is the par of the two issues; the $161.5M owed at Dec 31 1999 included about $45.1M of interest and $3.6M of financing costs, leaving about $112.8M of principal, a); Gateway "does not expect to be able to pay back" the county notes (FY2024 audit) -> public; repayment source not documented -> mixed. The 1990 bonds (~$148M, sin-tax backed per press) paid "primarily" for the stadium, so the earlier attribution of $100M of sin-tax bonds to the arena (PFM) is not used. Cavaliers advanced $7.8M for arena overruns, $7M later forgiven (private).
rows.lease_terms: Through 2033-34 season + two successive 5-yr TEAM options
rows.exit_penalty: Gateway owes Major Capital Repairs; told City/County it lacks funds

rows.public_construction_notes: City share capped at $125M, repaid by 2% hotel-occupancy + 5% car-rental taxes approved by voters (1998, 62,861-61,237) (Dallas Morning News 2006, c); teams (Hicks/Cuban) paid the rest. The Bond Buyer piece gives the 1998 bonds, $140.4M ($104.8M tax-exempt, $35.6M taxable), not the cap. The same 2006 article reports "more than $60 million in infrastructure and other public improvements" around the arena, $185.3M public through 2018 per the city (c, district-wide, not counted).
rows.lease_terms: Mavericks' lease at American Airlines Center expires in 2031
rows.exit_penalty: Mavericks pursuing a new arena on the former Valley View Mall site (June 2026)

rows.construction_cost_other_reports: Owner's completed "development and construction costs ... including financing costs" (Ascent 10-K405 FY1999). $169.1M 1998 budget incl. $5.7M contingency (b, Ascent 10-K405 FY1998); $160M "Total Project Cost" (b, DURA, scope not defined); $187M (c, Wikipedia)
rows.public_construction_notes: Denver Urban Renewal Authority: $36.5M developer reimbursement through TIF (demolition, remediation, site work; repaid 2016) + $4.5M City funds for public infrastructure. The 1997 Arena Agreement also gave: city title to the land with a 23-year ground lease back at $10 a year; payments based on the arena's property tax increment (the "rebates on property taxes for a 23-year term" in Ascent's FY1998 10-K, which appear to be the DURA reimbursement above, repaid in 2016, not a separate break); sales and use tax rebates during construction (amount not found); $2.25M of city business incentive payments during construction (s.5.9; relation to the $4.5M not established, not added); and exemption from the city's admissions (seat) tax (s.5.7; memo estimate only, not counted).
rows.tax_break_desc: Exemption from the Facilities Development Admissions ("seat") tax (1997 Arena Agreement s.5.7); 10% under the current code (DRMC 53-306, 2020), 1997 rate not confirmed
rows.tax_break_notes: Memo, not added: about $4M a year at McNichols (c, 9News; page returned 403, quote from search index only) x 24 seasons of the agreement's Operation Term (1999-2023) = $96M nominal (a); range $28M (7 seasons, to the end of the Nuggets' McNichols lease) to $108M (27 seasons to date)
rows.lease_terms: Team-affiliated owner; with the Oct 21 2024 rezoning and development agreement, the Nuggets and Avalanche agreed to remain in the area until June 30 2050 (c); penalty not found
rows.exit_penalty: n/a

rows.construction_cost_other_reports: Recorded historical cost of the arena building incl. Olympia-donated construction, excluding $8.4M of land (DDA FY2019 Note E). $934.9M construction in progress at completion incl. $8.4M land (b, FY2018); $938.0M building plus that land (a); $862.9M (c, Wikipedia); not the FY2021 MD&A "roughly $985 million", which adds all DDA land
rows.public_construction_notes: MSF Series 2014A $250M (repaid from DDA catalyst tax increment, incl. captured school taxes) + DDA Series 2017 $36M "to incentivize the Detroit Pistons to relocate" (NBA compliance). 2014B ($200M authorized, $188.5M drawn) was serviced by Olympia concession payments and retired by Olympia in 2017 -> private. Olympia donated land + construction valued at $47.8M.
rows.conduit_note: MSF Series 2014B: $200M authorized, $188.5M drawn, retired in 2017 through prepayment of base concession fees (b, DDA FY2018 Note G)
rows.bond_detail: 2014 Michigan Strategic Fund LO Revenue Bonds Series 2014A $250M tax-exempt | 2014 Michigan Strategic Fund Series 2014B $200M TAXABLE | 2017 Detroit DDA Series 2017 bonds (Pistons relocation work) $36M not confirmed | 2018 Detroit DDA Tax Increment Revenue Refunding Bonds Series 201 $287.425M not confirmed (refunds tax-exempt 2014A) | 2024 Detroit DDA Series 2024 bonds (refund the 2018A) $198.835M not confirmed (refunds 2018A)
rows.lease_terms: Pistons MOU with DDA (2016); 35-yr term widely reported but not verified (MOU PDF 403)
rows.exit_penalty: $36M 2017 DDA bonds to make arena NBA-compliant

rows.construction_cost_other_reports: Wikipedia figure tagged citation needed
rows.public_construction_notes: Privately financed building; the team bought the land. Public transit capital for the arena (b, SFMTA to OCII, Oct 20 2015): "nearly $61.9 Million" for four light-rail vehicles ($21.0M), a new center boarding platform ($24.9M), crossovers, power upgrades and signals; $19.4M from the Warriors' in-lieu transit impact fee (private), $7.96M from the General Fund (-> general) and $34.5M financed and repaid from the Mission Bay Transportation Improvement Fund, which holds General Fund revenue the project generates (-> tif). A plan, not an audited total: actuals found are four LRVs "not to exceed $15,875,000" (June 2017) and a supplemental appropriation for fiscal 2017-18 of $5.36M plus $0.63M (April 2016). City event-day costs (e.g., ~$2.5M/yr for parking control officers, SF Chronicle 2019; a General Fund deposit of at least $8.1M a year for event services under the ordinance) not counted.
rows.lease_terms: Team-owned
rows.exit_penalty: n/a

rows.construction_cost_other_reports: HCHSA "Arena Bonds" (Series 2001 G/H/I) $255.94M incl. garage & financing costs (b, lease; par, not cost); floor from primary budgets $195M = $175M Arena Budget + $20M city site and infrastructure cap (a)
rows.public_construction_notes: 2000 Letter Agreement: Sports Authority funds the $175M Arena Budget (+ garage + financing costs) from hotel-occupancy/car-rental-tax bonds; City acquires site (Marquette 2005: ~$20M land). Rockets pay overruns + up to $8M concessions, and their $8.5M/yr rent is pledged to a separate "Rent Supported Debt" issue that also financed construction, principal capped at $30.4M without the tenant's approval (b, lease App. A p.A-4) -> public figure overstates net public cost. City site and infrastructure money is a not-to-exceed $20M cash appropriation for "Site Acquisition and the Infrastructure Work" (b, 2000 Interlocal Arena Development Agreement s.2); no land/infrastructure split or funding stream stated -> infrastructure bucket. Public range in press: $125M-$175M.
rows.conduit_note: Rent Supported Debt backed by Rockets rent: principal capped at $30.4M without tenant approval (b, lease App. A p.A-4); a $57.54M 2014 taxable "Toyota Center Project" refunding is listed in the HCHSA debt worksheet, link to the rent-supported debt not confirmed
rows.lease_terms: Term = 360 months from Oct-2003 commencement (ends after 2032-33); no extension reported with Apr-2026 $180M renovation ($95M State of Texas)
rows.exit_penalty: Landlord duty to renovate to "first-class, state of the art" standard (s8.6) limited to Renovation Fund

rows.construction_cost_other_reports: $230.7M MCCRFA 1997A/B excise-tax lease rental bonds "to fund the construction of the Conseco Fieldhouse ... and an attached garage facility" (b, MCCRFA 2009 audit p.19; CIB FY2023 ACFR Note 5; par, not cost); $200M (Bond Buyer, search index only)
rows.public_construction_notes: $79M "from taxes" (Indiana Encyclopedia); PFM: local 43%, excise-tax lease-rental revenue (CIB hotel/F&B/admissions taxes). Conflict not resolved: the CIB says MCCRFA issued about $230.7M of 1997A/B excise-tax lease rental bonds "to fund the construction of the then Conseco Fieldhouse and an attached garage facility" (b, CIB FY2025 Note 5), more than the reported $183M cost, and that the lease rentals are paid from pledged state and local taxes; no primary split of public and private money was found, so the arena is counted in neither the privately nor the publicly built group.
rows.ongoing_notes: CIB "Fieldhouse operating expenses and reimbursements" + Pacers note-receivable forgiveness ($40M of 2010-13 operating loans forgiven 2015-24), 2014-2025 (ACFR ten-year tables), and the 2001 pass-through of cable franchise fees to the Pacers. 2002-2013 tables show no payment line; 1999-2000 not available (pre-GASB 34). Later tables restated 2017-18 upward by about $3.3M a year to include CIB-paid utilities, insurance and security (8.70 and 8.93 in the original ACFRs); 2014-16 were not restated, so they run low by about that much
rows.bond_detail: 2021 MCCRFA Excise Taxes Lease Rental Revenue Bonds Series 2021A  $401.41M not stated (5% coupons) | 2021 CIB Excise Taxes Revenue Subordinate Bonds Series 2021A $22.925M not stated (5%)
rows.lease_terms: 25-yr agreement 2019-2044 + 1-yr team option
rows.exit_penalty: Pacers may terminate if CIB fails to appropriate ~$12.5M/yr reimbursements or capital; Pacers owe up to $750M if they fail to play home games; if the Pacers and the CIB do not agree on more technology funding by 2036, the Pacers could terminate (IBJ 2019, c)

rows.construction_cost_other_reports: $1.8B (Bisnow 2021)
rows.public_construction_notes: Privately financed. Team bought publicly owned site parcels (city, FAA/LAWA, school district) for $66.25M; no appraisal found showing a below-market price.
rows.lease_terms: Team-owned
rows.exit_penalty: n/a

rows.public_construction_notes: Privately built on city-owned land. The City "entered into various agreements with the Arena Developer to advance approximately $70 million towards the project" (bonds for the arena, property conveyed and cash; b, CAO FY2022-23 budget p.379). Under the Gap Funding Agreement the developer owes the City that debt service and related costs, but the obligation is offset by credits, mainly the City's "Gross Receipts from Arena Admissions Fee" ($6.0M FY2022 est., $8.0M FY2023 budget) and incremental Convention Center parking revenue (same page), so the City's own revenue repays most of it -> public (mixed: admissions fee and parking revenue, split not documented). The developer pays shortfalls (in 2003, $16.5M including a $1.8M inducement; not netted). Seattle's 2017 evaluation: "$58 million in public financing in bonds and reserves", AEG as guarantor (c). Treated as conduit financing (not public money) until Oct 18, 2026.
rows.lease_terms: About 2041: the Lakers signed a 20-year lease extension with AEG about a year before Aug 2022 (Los Angeles Times via Yahoo, c); the exact end is not public
rows.exit_penalty: Not public

rows.construction_cost_other_reports: 2002 series A-E bond par $224.8M (GDG Table 2, from EMMA; par, not cost; larger than the $206M of bond proceeds applied to construction); Wikipedia $250M
rows.public_construction_notes: City CAFR FY2005: "The total construction cost of $250,000 [thousand] is to be funded from $186,000 from Senior Lien Revenue Bonds, $20,000 from Subordinate Lien Revenue Bonds, $12,000 each by the City and the County from non-ad valorem revenues, and $20,000 from the State of Tennessee for a parking structure and intermodal transfer station." Sports Authority bonds ($206M) are repaid from seat fees, state sales-tax rebates on Grizzlies-generated taxes (2001-2031), county car-rental fees, city and county hotel-motel taxes and MLGW in-lieu-of-tax payments (FY2015 CAFR; split not documented -> mixed). City $12M for site and infrastructure, to be repaid from hotel-motel taxes (-> tourist); County $12M (general); State $20M parking structure (general). Total includes site, infrastructure and the parking structure; no team contribution in the funding table.
rows.ongoing_notes: City+County flat operating subsidy $4.95M/yr (2021-25) rising to $6.3M/yr (2025-29) per PFM (c); paid per season (Action News 5, 2022), so five payments through the 2025-26 season; the 2026-27 season opened Oct 21 2026, after the as-of date (a). No primary record found: the only recurring city item of similar size, the New Memphis Arena Fund's $4.475M a year, is debt service on the construction bonds, so this series may double count capital
rows.lease_terms: Current lease ends after 2028-29 season; $550M renovation/new lease still unsigned as of Oct 16 2026 (the Oct 8 2026 Sports Authority agenda lists a construction agreement and a funding-agreement amendment; press reports approval)
rows.exit_penalty: (Attendance clause/2022 settlement already known - excluded)

rows.construction_cost_other_reports: Miami-Dade ACFR FY2025 notes p.79: "The construction of the Arena was funded 100 percent by the Miami Heat Limited Partnership ... The County capitalized $234.9 million of the cost of its construction" (same in FY2018). Alternatives: $213M (c, Wikipedia); $240M (c, Miami New Times); "cost over $200 million to construct" (b, Miami-Dade OIG IG11-34 p.5)
rows.public_construction_notes: County bought about 17 acres of waterfront land from the City of Miami for $37.6M in fall 1997, "in part" for the arena site (b, OIG IG11-34 p.2 and report p.9); the operator (BPL) financed and built the arena and recovers its cost through yearly amortization ($156.6M deducted through FY2010).
rows.ongoing_notes: County payments to the arena manager (BPL): $8.5M a year less $2.1M of American Airlines naming money = $6.4M net (1997 agreement); FY2000 $3.2M (half year); $5.0M pre-opening subsidy paid Oct 1998-Jul 1999 (OIG report p.13 note 2), booked in 1999; FY2001-10 $6.4M a year (a, from the Inspector General's $72.2M total); FY2011-12 not documented (contract $6.4M, not counted); FY2013-14 and FY2026 budgeted; FY2015-25 actual (ACFR liability reductions). The 2014 amendment fixes $6.4M through FY2029, then $8.5M a year July 2030-June 2035 (future, not counted) | County naming-rights payments to the arena manager: FTX and Kaseya deals: county pays BPL up to $2M a year through 2040; FY2021 $4.0M, FY2022 $2.0M (a), FY2023-25 $2.0M actual, FY2026 $2.0M budgeted | State of Florida sales-tax distribution to the operator (BPL, Ltd.), $166,667 a month for 30 years, Mar 1998-Mar 2028: OPPAGA 15-01 Exhibit B-2: $60M over 30 years, $32,500,070 paid through June 30 2014 (b), spread 1998 $1.5M (an April 1998 start is assumed: 195 payments by June 2014, although Exhibit B-2 says March), 1999-2013 $2.0M a year, Jan-Jun 2014 $1.0M; calendar years, while the county series uses fiscal years; later years at the scheduled $2.0M a year through Sept 2026 (a, actuals not verified). Not in the county figures
rows.lease_terms: Through June 30 2040 under the 2014 agreements (UPI; Commission Auditor notes, b); from 2025 either side may ask to renegotiate the terms for July 2035-June 2040 and, if either elects, terminate from July 1 2035
rows.exit_penalty: County subsidy $6.4M/yr (FY26 budget) rising to $8.5M 2031-35

rows.construction_cost_other_reports: $524.1M is the April 2016 development-agreement estimate incl. plaza, parking structure and an estimated $24.1M owner overrun (LFB); WCD recorded the arena at about $416M-$422M with $221.1M of private capital contributions (b/a, WCD 2018 audit Note 6), against $274.1M of private money in LFB; not reconciled
rows.public_construction_notes: WCD $203M = $108.1M appropriation bonds (state $4M/yr GPR grant + $4M/yr GPR offset by cut in Milwaukee County aid, to 2035-36) + dedicated-tax bonds ($54.3M + $37.9M refunding) from extended WCD room/F&B/car-rental taxes (residual $94.9M); City TIF $35M parking structure + $12M plaza. Bradley Center site conveyed to team free (value not documented).
rows.bond_detail: 2016 Wisconsin Center District appropriation revenue bonds $108.1M tax-exempt | 2016 WCD dedicated tax revenue bonds $54.3M tax-exempt | 2016 WCD dedicated tax revenue refunding bonds (Nov 29 2016) $37.9M tax-exempt (assumed) | 2016 WCD Subordinate Revenue Bonds Series 2016 (Taxable), BCPL pr $45M TAXABLE
rows.lease_terms: 30-yr lease (signed Apr 2016) + two 5-yr TEAM options; team may negotiate with third parties in last 5 yrs of term
rows.exit_penalty: Non-relocation damages of at least $553M in year 1, declining; the floor is reported as $20M (BizTimes) or $200M (WPR, quoting the district chair)

rows.construction_cost_other_reports: $104M construction + $23M city subsidy (LRL timeline); $126M = $104M private + $22M city land and infrastructure (b, 2003 Stadium Screening Committee packet p.3); $103M = $20M MCDA TIF bonds (public) + $80M team financing + a $3M MCDA loan repaid from team revenues (b, same packet, p.8 case study)
rows.public_construction_notes: OLA 2017 Exhibit 1: total initial cost $127M, public $23M (18%), "entirely of subsidies from the City of Minneapolis". The 2003 packet funds the public part with $20M of MCDA tax-increment bonds (p.8, -> tif) and says it bought $22M of land and infrastructure (p.3); it counts a $3M MCDA loan as private (repaid from team revenues). The other $3M of the OLA total has no documented stream (-> mixed). Built and owned privately (Ratner/Wolfenson) until 1995.
rows.ongoing_notes: City Operator Reimbursement to the arena operator (AEG), 2010-2018 actuals from adopted-budget financial plans (2011 may be the maximum rather than the amount paid). Not counted: transfers into the Arena Reserve fund ($4.602M in 2024 per the ACFR, the basis of the earlier PFM figure; $20.40M gross 2021-25), which also pay for capital and city administration; reimbursements for unamortized improvements in 2016-17 ($3.83M), likely inside the renovation; 1995-2009 and 2019-2025 operator payments not found
rows.lease_terms: Play through 2034-35 season (2016 agreement)
rows.exit_penalty: $50M payment to city if not fulfilled; $53.5M city debt service 2026-35

rows.construction_cost_other_reports: $84M (New Orleans Magazine). An earlier "$112M incl. site work (La. state presentation)" alternative had no URL and could not be located (Oct 16 2026), so it was dropped
rows.public_construction_notes: State-owned arena built by LSED on Superdome land before the NBA arrived (2002); paid with refinanced Superdome bonds backed by the LSED hotel-occupancy tax (New Orleans Magazine). Low-confidence split elsewhere ($50M state, $30M Hornets operating rights, $20M PSLs) not used.
rows.ongoing_notes: Audited LSED payments to the team outside the lease revenue split, by state fiscal year: naming-rights payments FY2003-05 and a FY2005 attendance credit; nonresident players' income tax passed through (FY2006 on); revenue-benchmark payments (FY2008, FY2010-11) and, from FY2012, the fixed additional annual payment (cash portions only; FY2012-13 deferrals went to the training facility); the state's $3.65M Quality Jobs equivalent for FY2025 and FY2026 (budgeted appropriations). Not counted: the $3.65M for FY2023-24 (obligation, no appropriation found), relocation-fee reimbursements, the suite-revenue payment ($4.89M FY2012-25) and home-game revenue entitlements. FY2026 audit not issued
rows.lease_terms: Initial term to June 30, 2029 (amended June 13, 2023); State agreement "set to expire in FY 2029"
rows.exit_penalty: State must keep paying $3.65M/yr Quality Jobs equivalent through FY2029

rows.public_construction_notes: Privately built and owned; 2011-13 ~$1B renovation privately funded (c).
rows.tax_break_notes: IBO (July 11, 2023): "more than $946.7 million (in 2023 dollars)" forgone, an estimate that "dates back to 1984 and not to 1982" and covers FY1984-FY2023 (full report p.9), converted to 2026 dollars from 2023; plus the Department of Finance's tax-expenditure values for FY2024 $42.2M, FY2025 $42.9M and FY2026 $43.3M (Annual Reports on Tax Expenditures), each converted from its year
rows.lease_terms: Arena license to June 30, 2055, fees +3%/yr
rows.exit_penalty: n/a

rows.public_construction_notes: Built with the MAPS (1993) one-cent sales tax before the NBA arrived.
rows.ongoing_notes: City operating subsidy to ASM Global for the Paycom Center: FY2023 only (City Auditor, Exhibit 3); other years are reported only combined with other city venues: $16.96M FY2022 and $15.64M FY2023 across ASM-managed facilities (OCPPA audited statements)
rows.lease_terms: Through at least 2053: 25 years from move-in to the new arena (KGOU 2025-06-18; Bond Buyer 2026-04-06); earlier reports said at least 2050
rows.exit_penalty: Early-exit penalties of up to $1B, declining over the term: $1B if the team leaves in the first five years after moving into the new arena, $850M in years 6-10, and a scale that continues for the 25 years (city release, June 17 2025); KGOU: "up to $1 billion"

rows.construction_cost_other_reports: Plan of finance (2016 restated interlocal, draft exhibit, not an audited final cost): $380M gross construction + $40M property, acquisition and site prep + $60M parking, roads and site improvements; Wikipedia: $380M arena + $100M land/infrastructure (c)
rows.public_construction_notes: Sources of funds, Event Center column (b): tourist development tax bonds $270M (senior $170M, subordinate $50M, completion $50M; capped at $270M of net proceeds, s.5.5) -> tourist; proceeds from the sale of city land $62M, City covenant bonds $37M and state and other government sources $30M -> general (the state's $2M-a-year sales-tax payment for 30 years, $60M nominal, OPPAGA 15-01, is bonded inside these lines and not added again); interest earnings $19M -> mixed (part of it accrued on the Magic's $50M deposit, s.5.4.3; not separable). The $12M "Present Value of Magic Use Payments" is city cash ("The City has provided $12 million in cash which is to be applied to the construction of the Events Center", s.5.4.8) that the Magic's use payments repay -> team-repaid financing, counted as private like Atlanta's and Detroit's team-serviced bonds and Cleveland's 2017 series (it was counted as public Oct 16-18, 2026). Public = $480M - Magic $50M - $12M = $418M (a); PFM counts $430M. The earlier split ($100M Community Redevelopment Agency tax increment + $330M tourist tax; Business View 2017) is not supported: CRA bonds appear only in the performing arts center column. Magic also guaranteed $100M of bonds.
rows.bond_detail: 2008 Orange County TDT / City of Orlando $342M tax-exempt
rows.lease_terms: Use Agreement ends June 30 2035 (2024 interlocal funding agreement, b); before the county issues its Contract Sixth Cent bonds (2027 at the earliest) the city must negotiate an extension at least as long as those bonds, with non-relocation penalties covering the remaining debt; the 2016 interlocal (s.5.4.7) also gives a five-year renewal option
rows.exit_penalty: Rent $1M/contract year

rows.construction_cost_other_reports: $206M often cited
rows.public_construction_notes: Privately financed by Snider/Spectacor; no public construction money found in sources reached. 2020-23 $400M renovation private (c).
rows.lease_terms: The 76ers plan to leave the arena when their lease expires in 2031 (Front Office Sports, c) and move to a new private South Philadelphia arena with Comcast Spectacor (target 2030-31)
rows.exit_penalty: Not public

rows.public_construction_notes: City $35M through bond sales (c, SBD 1995); Suns affiliate (PADLP) paid the rest. The city paid its share from a 1% hotel and 2% rental-car excise tax earmarked for a Sports Facilities Fund (b, 2019 council backup) -> tourist. A 1998 "Multipurpose Arena Refunding" of $48.74M (b, FY2007 CAFR) makes the $35M doubtful; the city says it invested about $80M in the arena through 2018, construction and later capital combined (b).
rows.lease_terms: Lease to 2037 (15 years beyond the old term), with a five-year option to 2042 at the team's discretion (council report, b)
rows.exit_penalty: Up to $200M in liquidated damages if the team relocates before the term ends (council report, b)

rows.public_construction_notes: City of Portland $34.5M; Allen $46M; $155M TIAA-CREF-led loan; $10M bond backed by box office/parking.
rows.bond_detail: 2027 State of Oregon debt (SB 1501, Oregon Laws 2026 ch. 74) - pl $365M planned
rows.lease_terms: Operating lease expires Oct 11 2030 unless extended (Resolution 37750 recital); the 2024 bridge agreement has a five-year option to extend through 2035 (City Ordinance 191857, per ACFR FY2024, b); new 20-yr lease + $573M public renovation under negotiation, definitive documents due by Dec 31 2026 (Resolution 37750)
rows.exit_penalty: City agreed not to enforce "first-class" maintenance duty during bridge (tolled); relocation needs City consent during term; team must repay City Contribution if it leaves; city ownership reduces property taxes collected by an estimated $1.2M a year (ACFR FY2024, b)

rows.construction_cost_other_reports: Construction monitor's last posted total project budget, incl. $34.5M land, 99.5% complete; excludes $49.2M of financing and other costs outside the construction budget and the ~$21M Kings-funded plaza. $507.1M estimate incl. $34.9M land and site and $11.3M financing costs (b, Aug 2015 official statement); $558.6M (b, monitor Report 31, Feb 2017); $558.2M (c, Wikipedia); $524.6M excluding land (a)
rows.public_construction_notes: City Contribution $223,130,100 = $220,426,649 of Series 2015 (federally taxable) lease-revenue bond proceeds + $2,703,451 other City moneys; City has no obligation beyond it. City also transferred development parcels/billboard rights (value not documented). City CAFR FY2017 records the arena as "sold to the Sacramento Kings" under the arena lease (sales-type lease accounting; minimum lease payments $407.7M over 36 years).
rows.bond_detail: 2015 Sacramento Public Financing Authority Lease Revenue Bonds Se $272.87M TAXABLE
rows.lease_terms: 35-yr non-relocation + two 5-yr extensions (term sheet); ~2051 inferred
rows.exit_penalty: Kings minimum lease payments $406.2M over 35 yrs

rows.construction_cost_other_reports: Recorded cost of the arena building and equipment in the county's Arena Venue fund, no land, probably incl. capitalized interest ($188,452,905 FY2006; $188,371,540 FY2010). $175M (c, Wikipedia text); $186M (c, infobox); 2000 venue bonds $148.845M par + Spurs $28.5M = $177.3M for the whole 2000 Project incl. Coliseum and grounds work (b/a)
rows.public_construction_notes: Venue-tax (hotel-occupancy and car-rental) bonds and cash (voters Nov 1999). Public = $188.4M recorded cost - Spurs $28.5M (b, 2019 official statement) = $159.9M (a). The recorded arena cost exceeds the $148.845M of 2000 bond proceeds plus the Spurs' $28.5M that funded the whole 2000 Project (arena, Coliseum, livestock facilities), so the public figure includes capitalized interest and venue-tax cash spent directly.
rows.bond_detail: 2000 Bexar County venue project bonds $169M tax-exempt
rows.lease_terms: Lease of the Frost Bank (AT&T) Center ends in 2032 (KSAT 2023); downtown arena targeted to open for the 2032-33 season (TPR 2025)
rows.exit_penalty: Break fees of up to $124M, depending on the year (KSAT 2023)

rows.construction_cost_other_reports: C$265M budget (MLGL); C$288M final; converted at 1999 avg 1.4858 CAD/USD (FRED EXCAUS)
rows.public_construction_notes: "No public funding was used" (arena history page). ~C$13M of nearby public infrastructure was built early with private financing. Site bought from Canada Post (federal Crown corp.) for C$60M; no evidence of below-market price.
rows.lease_terms: Team-affiliated owner
rows.exit_penalty: n/a

rows.construction_cost_other_reports: $66M Sumitomo loan (Deseret News 1991)
rows.public_construction_notes: Built privately by Larry H. Miller on RDA-owned land leased at $1/yr to 2060 (land value not documented for 1990; 2026 assessed land $68.77M, exempt). RDA cash/TIF help in 1990 reported but unverified (forum citing ~$18.7M) -> blank.
rows.bond_detail: 2025 Downtown Revitalization PID Sales Tax Revenue Bonds (SEG Red $899.99M tax-exempt
rows.lease_terms: 30-yr non-relocation tied to SLC 0.5% sales tax from 2025 (~2054-55 inferred)
rows.exit_penalty: If both teams leave, Smith Entertainment Group must repay the outstanding sales-tax bonds whose proceeds it received; if one team leaves, 50% of a $250M liquidated damages amount in years 1-15, reduced by $16,666,667 a year to zero at year 30, so $125M at most (draft participation agreement of July 5 2024, s.11.8(d), b; the executed agreement of Dec 10 2024 was not read)

rows.construction_cost_other_reports: Developer estimate "about $175 million" (b, GAO 1998); Pollin-funded building $200M (c); also reported $220M (c)
rows.public_construction_notes: GAO AIMD-98-223 Table 1 (Apr 30 1998): District predevelopment spending $61.49M, financed by arena-tax revenue bonds (a gross-receipts fee on D.C. businesses, ended FY2001): land $37.2M (-> land: bought with arena-tax bonds and contributed under the ground lease, the ledger's in-kind convention); Metro match $3.0M, employee relocation $4.0M, demolition, remediation and fees $15.1M, bank and issuance costs $2.2M (-> general). Plus a $12M federal transportation grant and $2M from WMATA for the Metro connection (-> general). Total $75.5M (a); District only $61.5M (b). The earlier ~$79M (c, Wikipedia) is not in any primary document reached. Building privately funded by Pollin.
rows.tax_break_desc: Real-property & possessory-interest tax exemption since construction, continued to June 2050 by the 2024 arena law (+ FY2025 deed transfer/recordation abatements)
rows.tax_break_notes: OCFO: $49.8M FY2025-28 + $262.9M FY2029-50; OCFO found the abatement not financially necessary
rows.bond_detail: 2025 DC capital budget FY2025-27 funded by GO bonds $515M not confirmed
rows.lease_terms: Lease-back to DCALP through June 30, 2050, with up to five 4-yr renewals; Wizards and Capitals must play home games there; no-shop to 2045
rows.exit_penalty: Damages not quantified in the fiscal impact statement

method: select a.team, a.construction_cost_other_reports, a.public_construction_notes, a.ongoing_notes, a.tax_break_desc, a.tax_break_notes, a.pilot_note, a.conduit_note, a.bond_detail, a.lease_terms, a.exit_penalty, a.lease_label, coalesce((select list(s.source_id order by s.ord) from arena_sources s where s.row_type = 'current_arena' and s.team = a.team and s.field = 'property_tax_source'), []) as property_tax_sources, coalesce((select list(s.source_id order by s.ord) from arena_sources s where s.row_type = 'current_arena' and s.team = a.team and s.field = 'lease_source'), []) as lease_sources, coalesce((select list(s.source_id order by s.ord) from arena_sources s where s.row_type = 'current_arena' and s.team = a.team and s.field = 'tax_break_source'), []) as tax_break_sources from arenas a order by a.team
